articles.title: How .raw reworked STOW's identity to make its coffee roasting visible
articles.summary: Slovenian branding studio .raw has redesigned specialty coffee company STOW's identity to communicate the scientific precision behind its sourcing, roasting, and testing processes. The system retains STOW's original factory-inspired symbol while introducing a geometric wordmark, Aeonik Mono typography, structured layouts, and square brackets borrowed from scientific notation. A restrained black, white, and gray palette is complemented by five accent colors representing different flavor profiles, making the brand's technical expertise and sensory qualities visible across packaging, menus, and other applications.

articles.title: Google tests sticky citations in desktop AI Overviews
articles.summary: Google is testing a new desktop AI Overview interface that keeps source citations visible as users scroll through AI-generated answers. The citations move with the content instead of disappearing offscreen, making it easier to access supporting websites while reading longer responses. The experiment also introduces a horizontal divider separating the AI Overview from conventional search results, and the design has been spotted across multiple browsers.

articles.title: Spotify's New Tool Aims to Stop Deepfakes from Being Attributed to Real Artists
articles.summary: Spotify is rolling out Artist Profile Protection to all artists, letting them review and remove releases submitted under their name after an eight-month beta. Artists get alerts when new music appears under their name, and an advanced setting holds releases until they manually approve them. The launch follows Billboard's report that Sony Music sought removal of more than 260,000 deepfake songs from digital platforms.

articles.title: AI is the New Old Design Material
articles.summary: Designers have always learned their medium by working it, and AI models are the next material. A mockup shows one sample, while a model returns a distribution of answers that only sampling code reveals. Running each prompt 50 times, bringing the worst answers to design review, and saving failures as shared test cases puts that spread in front of the team.

articles.title: AI Sped up the Build: How Can Accessibility Testing Keep Up?
articles.summary: AI has sped up planning, design, and development, but only 30% of professionals in Level Access' survey of 2,500+ report gains in QA and testing. WebAIM found detected errors per home page rose 10.1%, while organizations that keep improving use AI at the same rate but invest more in training and culture. Accessibility judgment moves earlier through annotated handoffs, gated pull requests, and AI-drafted fixes reviewed in context, each leaving a regression test behind.

articles.title: Your path to design engineering
articles.summary: Design engineering combines the ability to solve design problems with responsibility for implementing those solutions, but the skills needed depend on whether someone comes from design, frontend engineering, or a different background. Frontend engineers can develop design judgment by exploring alternative layouts and understanding visual hierarchy, while designers can learn to translate their decisions into functional interfaces and handle real-world implementation constraints. This choose-your-own-adventure learning guide offers practical exercises for each starting point, emphasizing small projects, iterative practice, and understanding the reasoning behind design and engineering decisions.

articles.title: Design Engineering Has a Handoff Problem
articles.summary: AI-generated components from designers were meant to lighten engineers' load, but ones with hardcoded values and inline SVGs now pile up in engineers' review queues. The handoff has simply moved down a level, with designers lacking the governance, permissions, and shared tooling engineering built over years. The fix starts with holding designer code to the same merge bar, running deterministic checks before human review, and giving designers a lighter environment.

articles.title: Prevent UX Theater with Cross-Functional Collaboration
articles.summary: UX theater occurs when organizations perform design activities without meaningfully involving users or allowing research to influence decisions. Cross-functional collaboration can help counter this by bringing designers, researchers, developers, and other stakeholders into shared discussions about user needs and product priorities. Meaningful collaboration requires teams to move beyond workshops and deliverables toward evidence-based decisions, shared accountability, and genuine participation in the design process.

articles.title: AI's Role in the Creative Process
articles.summary: Debates pitting AI enthusiasts against skeptics miss the real question: which parts of creative work to automate and which to keep. Tedious labor like VFX green-screen cleanup can go, but friction such as trimming a shot or drafting a brief is where thinking happens. Figma's Gaussian splat campaign, generated with Seedance 2.5 in Weave, still took long rounds of riffing before its shots felt finished.

articles.title: Disney's Radical New Animation Technique Will Make Hexed the End of an Era
articles.summary: Hexed may be the last original Disney film in the studio's familiar 3D style, as every original from Clay onward gets its own look.

articles.title: Artists and creators are leaving Etsy in droves over its new AI policy
articles.summary: Artists and independent sellers are closing their Etsy stores after forthcoming terms explicitly authorize the platform and its partners to use seller content for AI training, testing, and development, despite Etsy's assurances that it does not train models to copy or replace creators' work.

articles.title: How to experiment when designing in a regulated field like Healthcare UX
articles.summary: Rapid experimentation is increasingly accessible through AI tools, but designers working in healthcare and finance face strict regulations around sensitive data, privacy, and product safety.
